Office Visit - Follow-up
Patient: Nils Szabo | DOB: 04/13/1976 | MRN: SYN-6833801
Date of service: 08/04/2025 | Dr. Petra Cordero, MD

History of present illness:
49-year-old man seen for follow-up of low back pain. He first noticed the pain shooting down his left leg after a fall on ice, nearly three months before this visit.

Treatment to date:
Two months of supervised exercise sessions plus over-the-counter anti-inflammatories have not brought lasting relief.

History:
Past medical history: hypertension, seasonal allergies.
Medications: lisinopril 10 mg daily; loratadine 10 mg daily.

Review of systems:
Red flag screen negative: denies bowel or bladder dysfunction, saddle anesthesia, fever, unexplained weight loss, or history of cancer.

Physical exam:
Back: tenderness over the lower lumbar paraspinal muscles; straight-leg raise positive on the left at 45 degrees.
He cannot rise onto his toes on the left as well as on the other side, the ankle jerk is reduced on the left, and touch feels dull along the outer edge of that foot.

Assessment and plan:
Assessment: left S1 lumbar radiculopathy.
Plan: MRI lumbar spine without contrast to evaluate for disc herniation; home exercise program; follow up after imaging.
